title: The eleven days — Meera, 38 (PMDD is biology)
caption:
Eleven days a month she didn't recognize herself. PMDD is in the DSM-5. Track daily for 2 cycles — the DRSP chart (IAPMD) is what a doctor can actually read.
Which day does yours start?
www.aiforheratx.org
#pmdd #womenshealth #pmddawareness #cycletracking #hormonehealth

scenes.text: Two good weeks, then eleven days I don't *recognize* myself.
Meera, 38, yelled about one missing shoe, then cried in the parked car before walking back in.
phrases: Meera, 38. Two kids, a job she likes.
Then cried in the parked car before walking back in smiling.

scenes.text: Everyone had a theory. Not one of them was 'this has a name and a diagnosis.'
phrases: Just PMS, we all get it.
It stops the day my period starts. Every single month.

scenes.text: About 1 in 20 menstruating women have PMDD — a recognized diagnosis, not a mood (IAPMD).

scenes.text: At NIMH they switched the ovarian hormones off and her symptoms stopped; switched them back on, symptoms returned.
phrases: At NIMH they switched the hormones *off*.
Switched them back on — the symptoms came back.
Same hormones as everyone else. Her brain just answers louder.

scenes.text: Two cycles of daily ratings, plus a 20-minute walk most days — WHO asks for 150 minutes a week.
phrases: Rate your 3 worst symptoms 0-3 before bed. That's the DRSP (IAPMD).
Two cycles of that chart is what a doctor can actually read.
Calcium beat placebo for PMS in a 1998 trial — ask yours before adding anything.
And talk to yourself like you'd talk to a friend. — Kristin Neff, Self-Compassion
